CLOSED: DECLINED WITH EVIDENCE (owner decision 2026-10-01, in chat). The pre-registered confirmation (frozen d4e2280a, manifest b37f83fa) declined all three candidates. Report: docs/verification/group-bootstrap-confirmation-20260930.md on group/bootstrap-harness-20260930 @ b06c4b1e.
Why:
(1) Where native PM/mKH is already calibrated, the bootstrap is slightly conservative, and in C-n20-DI-Vspread-T0-N8 that cost more power than the non-loss margin allows. Null: native .0507 vs B-EB .0428. Power: native .384 vs B-plug .347 and B-EB .351. Pre-registered definite-loss rule.
(2) In the original failure cell C-n80-DG-Vrev-T0-N8 the bootstrap roughly halves the excess but cannot certify it within .065. Native .0936; B-plug .0647 and B-EB .0694 are Unresolved. Equal-subject HC3 is calibrated at .0512.
(3) At n=8 with tau2>0 (C-n8-DG-Vspread-T2-N40) the bootstrap inflates where native does not: .065-.067 vs .046.
Diagnosis: incidental-variance nuisance. With nu=8, the per-subject variance estimates are too noisy, and in the reversed design they are structured, so neither the plug-in variances nor one exchangeable Smyth prior reproduces the true joint law of (y, v). A small-n PM tau2 fit also under-disperses u*. This matches the declaration's warning that bootstrap refinement theorems do not hold here.
Candidate directions, not scheduled: a marginal t-likelihood that integrates sigma_i^2 (the declaration's alternative); design-aware variance modelling; or HC3/sandwich inference for structured-heterogeneity cases.
